title: What Is Thompson Submachine Gun? — Definition
body:

title: Origins and History of Thompson Submachine Gun
body:
The Thompson Submachine Gun belongs to the 1921–1940s era and traces to Auto-Ordnance.

The torsion catapult and ballista armed Rome; the trebuchet (12th c.) perfected gravity artillery, throwing 150-kg stones at castles. The longbow (Crécy, 1346; Agincourt, 1415) ended the armored knight's dominance; gunpowder (China, then Europe by 1300s) replaced them all. Matchlocks (1400s), wheellocks, then flintlocks (1600s) armed musketeers; the socket bayonet (1700s) made pikemen obsolete. Smoothbore cannon — bronze then iron — sieged and ship-fought for 400 years; rifling and the Minié ball (1840s) made the Civil War rifle-musket lethal at 500 yards. Smokeless powder (1880s) ended this era.

Within that longer story, Thompson Submachine Gun: The 1921; the 1.75M. The Tommy is the gangster's gun.

db_name: The Thompson Submachine Gun Signature Database
title: How Thompson Submachine Gun Works
body:
Torsion engines twist sinew/hair skeins to store energy; the trebuchet drops a counterweight to whip a sling. Bows store energy in bending limbs; the crossbow's spanning mechanisms (cranequin, windlass) multiply the soldier's strength. Matchlocks lower a burning cord to a priming pan; wheellocks spin serrated steel against pyrite; flintlocks strike flint on steel, showering sparks. Smoothbore muskets fire round balls with windage; rifling spins the Minié ball for accuracy. Black powder (saltpeter/charcoal/sulfur) burns fast and smoky — the white battlefield cloud.

Applied to the Thompson Submachine Gun (1921–1940s, Auto-Ordnance): The Tommy is the gangster's gun.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Anatomy of Thompson Submachine Gun — Components
body:
Every Thompson Submachine Gun is an assembly of the historical military technology family's standard parts:

• Skein / torsion bundle — Twisted sinew storing catapult energy.
• Throwing arm & sling — Trebuchet/catapult launch system.
• Counterweight — Gravity engine of the trebuchet.
• Bowstave / prod — Longbow limb or crossbow prod.
• Lock mechanism — Match, wheel, or flint ignition.
• Barrel — Smoothbore tube; touch-hole to percussion.
• Bayonet — Plug then socket; the infantryman's spear.
• Cannon & carriage — Bronze/iron tube on field or naval carriage.
• Powder & shot — Black powder charges; round shot, canister.
• Armor plate — Proofed breastplates; the arms race with guns.

When examining a surviving Thompson Submachine Gun, identify these parts in order: Skein / torsion bundle, Throwing arm & sling, Counterweight, Bowstave / prod, Lock mechanism, Barrel.

title: Thompson Submachine Gun Restoration Guide
body:
Conservation, not shooting restoration, for most pieces. Oil and wax for steel; leather care for scabbards. Document markings. Consult museums for significant artifacts.

Restoration order for a Thompson Submachine Gun: 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical military history record without a current-limited bring-up.

title: Thompson Submachine Gun — Trebuchet range physics (Runnable Python)
body:
Estimates trebuchet projectile range from counterweight energy — the siege engineer's physics, demonstrated safely as mathematics.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Thompson Submachine Gun so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Trebuchet physics (public-domain mechanics; math demonstration only)
import math

def trebuchet_range(counterweight_kg, drop_m, projectile_kg, efficiency=0.35):
    # energy = m*g*h * efficiency -> projectile velocity -> range at 45deg
    e = counterweight_kg * 9.81 * drop_m * efficiency
    v = math.sqrt(2 * e / projectile_kg)
    return v**2 / 9.81  # 45-degree range

r = trebuchet_range(6000, 8, 50)
print(f"6-ton counterweight, 8m drop, 50kg stone: ~{r:.0f} m range")
print("(Warwolf-class engines reportedly threw 140kg+ stones hundreds of meters)")
# Longbow energy for comparison
print(f"\nlongbow (~150 lbf draw, 30in): ~{150*4.448*0.762/2:.0f} J stored (approx)")
